questions.question: Enlarge a 4 × 6 rectangle by a scale factor of 2 and reduce it by ½. Compare the shapes with the original.
questions.expected_answer: 8 × 12 and 2 × 3. Both are similar to the original: same shape and angles, every length multiplied by the same factor.

questions.question: Compare the perimeter and area of the 4 × 6 rectangle with its enlargement by factor 2.
questions.expected_answer: Perimeter 20 → 40 (× 2); area 24 → 96 (× 4), because both length and width double.

questions.question: How do you enlarge a sloping line on squared paper? Explain why.
questions.expected_answer: Count its horizontal and vertical steps and multiply each by the scale factor (e.g. 2 across, 2 up → 4 across, 4 up), which keeps the slope and angle the same.
